newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist mayor on trial for anti-Israel rally.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist mayor on trial for anti-Israel rally.

text.p: A Turkish state security court on Thursday began the trial of a former mayor from the ruling Welfare Party on charges of serious public order offences for organising an anti-Israeli protest, a defence lawyer said.
"The trial began today. Our request for the release of defendant Bekir Yildiz was rejected," lawyer Mehmet Ali Bulut told Reuters.
Yildiz enraged secularists by hosting a night of anti-Israel protests in Ankara's Sincan district in January which were regarded as a call for the implementation of Islamic "Sharia" law.
Yildiz and Iranian ambassador Ali Reza Bagheri spoke on a stage draped with a banner of the late leader of the militant Palestinian group Islamic Jihad Fathi Shqaqi.
The lawyer said Yildiz was accused of "providing aid to an armed gang and making its propaganda" and faced three to five years in jail if found guilty.
In Turkey, the accusation of aiding an illegal group is a catch-all charge often used against civilians suspected of militant Islamist or Kurdish sentiment.
Ten others who took part in the protest were charged with similar offences but four of them were allowed to leave the jail at Tuesday's hearing, the lawyer said.
Tanks toured Sincan several days after the Jerusalem protest in an apparent warning to Islamists from the secularist army.
Welfare leader Necmettin Erbakan, under pressure from the military, has toned down his rhetoric since becoming Turkey's first Islamist prime minister last June.
